haiku-low.q1: Step 4, after checks and before any new instance starts. The live release must still work on the migrated schema, since migrations are additive.
haiku-low.q2: Only in a later release, after the release still using the old column or table has been retired (step 11 of the replacing deploy).
haiku-low.q3: Each of 4 instances must pass 3 consecutive /healthz checks, then smoke tests, before gate_deadline (10 min). Else Abort: new colour to 0.
haiku-low.q4: At step 8, the public listener is repointed from the old target group to the new one in one change; old colour finishes in-flight requests.
haiku-low.q5: 5xx rate above 1% in a 5-minute window after switch. Rollback repoints listener to old colour, scales new colour to 0, alerts team; migrations never reversed.
haiku-low.q6: Until T+30 min; after that no fast switch back. Later problems need a normal deploy of the previous release through this checklist.
haiku-low.q7: Transaction failure: schema unchanged. Index failure: invalid index dropped, additive changes stay. New colour never starts; run fails at step 12.
haiku-low.q8: Step 2 reads the public listener's target group: that colour is live, the other is new. The listener is the only lasting record.
haiku-low.q9: A CI concurrency group (deploy-catalog-web): one run holds it and later runs queue. The run keeps it from step 1 until step 12.
haiku-low.q10: Smoke tests run through an internal CI-only test listener pointed at the new colour's target group; users stay on live colour.
haiku-low.q11: The pipeline runs one migrate task from the new image against the shared database. Instances never migrate on startup, so migrations run exactly once per deploy.
haiku-low.q12: Scaled to 0 and left empty. Next deploy's step 2 scales any colour still running instances to 0 before using it.

sonnet.q1: Step 4, after build/check (step 3) and before any new-release instance exists (step 5). The live colour (old release) must keep working on the migrated schema.
sonnet.q2: Only in a later release, after the release that still used the old column/table has been retired (step 11 of the deploy that replaced it).
sonnet.q3: All 4 instances must each pass 3 consecutive /healthz checks (checked every 10s), then the smoke tests must pass, all before gate_deadline (step 5 time + 10 minutes). If not, Abort: scale new colour to 0, leave public listener alone, go to step 12 (failed).
sonnet.q4: In step 8, the public listener is repointed from the old target group to the new one in a single change; new requests go to the new colour while in-flight requests on the old colour finish.
sonnet.q5: Trigger: the public listener's 5xx rate over a rolling 5-minute window goes above 1% during the watch (T to T+15). Engineers can also start the rollback job from T onwards. Rollback repoints the public listener to the old colour's target group, scales the new colour to 0 and alerts the team; it never reverses migrations (schema stays as migrated).
sonnet.q6: Until step 11 at T+30 min (when the old colour is scaled to 0). Problems found during the hold (T+15 to T+30) are handled by an engineer starting the rollback job. After T+30 there is no fast switch back; you do a normal deploy of the previous release through this checklist.
sonnet.q7: For table/column migrations: the single transaction rolls back, schema unchanged. For an index build failure: the invalid index is dropped, the committed table/column changes stay, and the unrecorded index migration reruns in the next deploy. Either way the deploy stops, the new colour is never started, the live colour keeps serving, and the run goes to step 12 (failed).
sonnet.q8: Step 2 reads which target group the public listener forwards to: that colour is live, the other is new. Recorded in the load balancer's public listener (the only lasting record); this run also writes live_colour and new_colour to pipeline run variables, discarded when the run ends.
sonnet.q9: A CI concurrency group (e.g. deploy-catalog-web): one run holds it, later runs queue. The run keeps the slot from step 1 until step 12 (Finish), or until CI releases it if the run dies.
sonnet.q10: Through an internal test listener (reachable only from CI, e.g. port 8443) pointed at the new colour's target group, while the public listener still forwards to the live colour.
sonnet.q11: One `migrate` task run by the pipeline from the new image against the shared database (step 4). Instances never migrate on startup, so migrations run exactly once per deploy.
sonnet.q12: They are scaled to 0 (the new colour is idle and empty). If the scale-down fails, the team is alerted. Step 2 of the next deploy scales that colour to 0 before using it, and the colour left with 0 instances is the one the next deploy goes into.
